, in its broadest sense, the picturesque aesthetic is the imitation and reproduction of the picturesque, and the picturesque is the imitation and production of nature, and nature is the imitation and creation of the picturesque, in a never-ending cycle.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the picturesque is an eclectic style that aims to capture and reproduce the qualities of a real, but ideal, landscape.
it is a study of the relationship between the picturesque and the suburban, with an emphasis on the role played by the picturesque in the development of the suburban aesthetic.

the picturesque eclecticism in the suburban landscape of Bedford Park, England, and in the writing of Morris, represents the failure of vision of the middle class to produce a utopian community in the nineteenth century.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the picturesque is a style, a way of looking, and a set of social and political ideals.
the picturesque is a style that can be used by the middle class to create a utopia that is both aesthetically and socially pleasing.
